**Shipped — build 182 is live at miso.nøøb.org, and the transcript distribution gap is closed.** The push notification already went out to your phone.

The node is **`mirrored-words`**, a subfeature of `/mirror`: transcripts are now part of the mirrored record. What I built and proved:

- **Words travel eagerly, like metadata.** A new `TranscriptShared` message rides the persistent outbox; the exchange keeps a per-user `words.json` beside the blob index and broadcasts improvements to your other instances. In the two-instance test, a transcript made on instance A appeared on instance B **live, with no reload**, attached to the dimmed remote tile.
- **The laptop reseed bug is fixed too.** `RecList` still wipes stamps on boot, but the `RecIndex` catch-up reply now arrives with words already stamped on its items — so the laptop stops re-deriving what the phone already said. Proved by reloading instance A: its local re-transcribe of my garbage test audio failed (empty stamp), then catch-up restored the real words and the scheduler went idle.
- **Collisions follow `/phone`'s better-replaces-rough rule**, with one honest amendment discovered during testing: at equal grade, real words beat the empty stamp a failed local attempt leaves behind — otherwise a device whose own attempt failed would refuse words another device actually made. Empty transcripts never travel. A grade-2 upgrade on A replaced B's grade-1 live.
- **The ordering race closes itself**: words arriving at the exchange before their recording's announcement get folded into the announcement's metadata (proved with curl — a `TranscriptShared` for an unannounced id, then its `RecShared`, produced an index entry carrying the words).
- **Toggle proven**: unticked, the composed output drops all trace of the node and the app runs as before; re-ticked and rebuilt.

One nice retroactive effect: when your phone picks up build 182, its announcer will notice the transcript from yesterday's field test still sitting in its state and share it — so those words should finally reach the laptop without you re-recording anything.

**Shipped — build 183 is live, and the release list now shows only real changes.**

What ash saw was the awaiting-update review section: it deliberately shows a release line for any pending build no feature row represents ("an update never lists nothing"), and the diary commits — `handover:`, `notes:`, `idea:` — were landing there since they're counted builds too. The fix is a new node, **`bookkeeping`**, under `/policy` (which owns the release-classification doctrine; `/review` is at its child cap):

- **The deploy classifier gains a third kind, `docs`**: a commit whose every touched file is root-level markdown or `transcripts/` changed nothing on any device. Dry-run against real history classified all six diary commits as `docs` while keeping real releases as `feature`/`fix` — and the live changes.json now confirms it.
- **Entries stay in the file** — build numbers are commit counts and `/policy`'s fixes-mode coverage check needs the numbering gap-free — they just carry their honest kind. A pleasant side effect: doc-only builds now correctly auto-apply under the `fixes` policy, since a `docs` commit is never a `feature`.
- **`/review` got a small behaviour-preserving refactor**: its release-line filter now routes through a `releaseWorthy(entry)` seam (base accepts everything, spec updated with a revision note), and the bookkeeping node redefines it to refuse `docs`. Proved at runtime: `docs → false`, `fix`/`feature → true`; unticked and relinked, the node's code leaves the page and all entries are worthy again — old behaviour intact.
